title: Gate stall watchdog kills a cold debug build during long links (v0.27.0 cut gate)

labels.name: bug

labels.name: source:agent

labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
The v0.27.0 cut gate (cut.yml, stage gate, 2026-11-26 00:17Z) stopped at step [01] "debug build (--no-run)" after 22.2 min. No test ran and none failed (summary: "0 failed, 1 stalled").

What happened: the step compiled until about 00:25Z. Then three `rust-lld` links ran at the same time (the `camcraft-ui` test binaries, cold build, `-j 4`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`). The links wrote no output for 15 min. The stall watchdog (`xtask/src/watchdog.rs`, default 15 min for a debug step, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` not set) then killed the process tree. The tag stage was skipped.

Why it is a bug: a `--no-run` build step is a build, not a test. A cold link of a large test binary can be silent for longer than a test step. The watchdog cannot tell a slow link from a hang, so a cut on a cold runner can fail with no code fault.

Possible fixes (choose one):
1. Give build steps (`--no-run`) the longer limit that `--release` and `--ignored` steps already get (4x).
2. Count child-process CPU time (rustc, rust-lld, cc) as progress, and stall only when the tree is idle.
3. Set `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` for the gate step in `cut.yml` (a workaround, not a fix).

Workaround for the current cut: re-run the gate with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN=45` in the cut runner's environment.

Related: #3493 (how the watchdog kills a step; this issue is about when).

Done means: a cold release-tier gate on the cut runner passes step [01] without a stall, and a unit test in `xtask` pins the build-step limit.

title: Heidenhain posts: write the dialect of the control and NC software stated in the machine file

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Goal

HEIDENHAIN controls accept different program words per control and per NC software version. Today:
- the Klartext post accepts only iTNC 530 NC 340490-03;
- the DIN/ISO post writes words that are valid only on newer software (#4093, #4094).

The posts should read the control facts that the machine file already states and write the matching dialect. A control or version that a post cannot serve is refused by name.

## The machine file (no new field)

`controller.identity` already holds the facts (#3181, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`):

```json
"controller": {
  "post": "Heidenhain Klartext",
  "identity": { "model": "iTNC 530", "nc_software": "340490-03", "installed_options": ["1", "19"] }
}
```

Proposal: keep the file to facts only. Make the values canonical:
- `model`: as HEIDENHAIN writes it (`TNC 320`, `iTNC 530`, `TNC 640`, `TNC7`, ...).
- `nc_software`: 6-digit ID, `-`, 2-digit release, optional ` SP<n>`.
- `installed_options`: HEIDENHAIN option numbers as strings.

A missing `installed_options` means "unknown": the post refuses or warns for functions that need an option.

## Capability flags (derived from model + NC software + options)

One shared resolver gives each post a flag set. The main flags, each with its HEIDENHAIN version source in the research notes:

- `language.iso`: DIN/ISO exists (none on TNC 124/128/310; TNC 320 from 340 55x-04; TNC 620 from 340 56x-02; TNC 426/430 from 280 472; TNC7 from 81762x-17).
- `blockForm`: `contour`, or `paraxial` for TNC 124/128 (one axis per block, no arcs): refuse.
- `decimals`: 3 (TNC 124/310/410) or 4.
- `toolCallByName`, `toolNameMax` (16, or 32 from TNC 640 34059x-02), `toolDefLR` (false on TNC7 from 81762x-19).
- `drill.c200` / `drill.c205`: the cycle parameter level. Q379/Q253 from iTNC 340 422. Q208/Q395 only from iTNC 60642x-04, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-05.
- `oldCycles`: cycles 1/2/17 definable, run-only (iTNC from 340 422) or absent.
- `preset.cycle247`: cycle 247 sets a datum value before iTNC 340 422, and activates a preset-table row after it.
- `dwell`: cycle 9 / `G04 F`, or `FUNCTION DWELL` (TNC 640 -07, TNC 620 -04, TNC 320 -04, TNC7; never on iTNC 530).
- `tilt` (none / cycle 19 / PLANE), `planeAxial`, `planeSym`; `tcpm.kt` / `tcpm.iso` (M128 or FUNCTION TCPM; ISO FUNCTION TCPM only from TNC 640 34059x-10 / TNC 620 81760x-07).
- `m140`, `m136m137`, `feedFzFu`, `arcs.spatial`, `arcs.helixLin`, `q.qs`, `q.qlqr`, `q.formulaPriority2020` (TNC 640 34059x-11: always write parentheses).
- Option gating: tilting needs option 8 (iTNC: 1), TCPM option 9 (iTNC: 2), and on TNC 620 cycles 201-205/208/209 need option 19.

The profile table (control and version range to flag values) is in the research notes. It covers TNC 310, 410, 426/430, iTNC 530 (four profiles), TNC 320, TNC 620, TNC 640 and TNC7.

## What the posts branch on

- **Klartext:** profile check (replaces the fixed 340490-03 check), tool call form, the `M140` retract or `L Z.. M91/M92`, cycle 247, dwell form, and later the drilling cycles and the cycle parameter level.
- **DIN/ISO:** refuse when `language.iso` is false; the G200/G205 parameter level; always `G04 F` for a dwell unless `FUNCTION DWELL` is confirmed for ISO programs; `G247` only with the preset-table meaning; the coordinate format.

## Scope and order

1. The resolver and flags in one place (post engine or a shared post helper), with a table test: control + version → flags.
2. The DIN/ISO post uses it for the fixes in #4093 and #4094 (these can land first with a narrow check, and move to the resolver here).
3. The Klartext post uses it, and serves more than 340490-03.
4. A refusal by name for an unknown model or version (no silent fallback, because cycle 247 changes meaning between versions).

## Done means

- The resolver maps each control/version in the profile table to its flags. A table test pins it.
- Both posts branch on the flags, not on fixed version strings.
- An unknown control or version is refused by name.
- The goldens of the shipped Picomax machine file do not change, except for the fixes of #4093 and #4094.

Source: HEIDENHAIN's public manuals and "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents, collected and compared by the author's agent (notes, not in the repository). Related: #3095, #3181, #4085, #4086, #4087, #4088, #4093, #4094.

## What happens

`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:744-747`:
- G200 writes `Q395=+0`.
- G205 writes `Q379`, `Q253`, `Q208=+99999.999` and `Q395`.

## Which versions accept which parameters

From HEIDENHAIN's own change lists and cycle manuals:

- **Q379, Q253** (cycle 205): from iTNC 530 NC 340 422, TNC 640 -01, TNC 620 340 56x-01, TNC 320 34055x-06. **Valid on 340 490.**
- **Q208** (cycle 205) and **Q395** (cycles 200 and 205): only from iTNC 530 **60642x-04**, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-05 (Q395 in cycle 200: 77185x-01). Source: "Cycle 205: Input parameter Q208 for retraction feed rate added" (iTNC 530 manual 670388-25, p. 13; 737759-24, p. 20).

So the post's G200 and G205 blocks are not valid on any iTNC 530 340 49x software. This includes the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (NC 340490-03). The programming station used in #3095 runs 606425-04, which is why it accepted the blocks.

Note: the iTNC 60642x-04 change list names the depth reference "Q359", but the example blocks of the same manuals show `Q395`. This is probably a typo in the list.

## Expected

- For iTNC 530 340 49x (and other controls before the versions above), write G200 without Q395, and G205 without Q208 and Q395.
- The control's dwell or retract defaults then apply, or the post refuses a requested behaviour that the old cycle cannot do, by name.
- The choice follows the control and NC software in the machine file (see the dialect issue filed with this one).

## Done means

- G200 and G205 for an iTNC 530 340 49x machine contain only the parameters of that software.
- A test pins both parameter sets.
- The changed goldens are listed in the PR.

Related: #3095.

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:post

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## What happens

On a tool change, `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:381-392` writes only `T<n> G17 S..` and then `M3`. It writes no retract, no `M6` and no `M0`. The next block is `G00 G40 G90 Z+<clearance>` with the length of the **new** tool.

The engine does not refuse this. `crates/post/src/post/machine_installation.rs:67-68` only passes `toolChangeMode` to the script, and the DIN/ISO post never reads it.

## Why it is wrong on the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03)

- The machine has a manual tool change (`assets/machines/fehlmann-picomax55.mch`).
- The machine's programming manual changes a tool with `L Z+0 R0 FMAX M92`, then an XY park move with `M6`. TOOL CALL comes before the M6 move (manual p. 2-11 and p. 2-19).
- The machine parameters from the delivery CD (the machine parameter file) confirm it:
  - MP 7440 bit 0 = 0: the program halts at M06.
  - MP 7480.0 = 1: TOOL CALL only passes the T number to the PLC. TOOL CALL does not stop the program.
  - MP 950 / MP 4210.0: the tool-change height is M92 Z-0.05.

A multi-tool DIN/ISO program therefore runs on with the old tool in the spindle, and the new tool's length and speed are active. This gives a wrong Z and a possible crash.

The machine file selects the Klartext post, which stops with `M0`. The defect occurs when a user selects the DIN/ISO post for a manual-change machine.

## Expected

One of:
- The DIN/ISO post refuses by name when `toolChangeMode` is a manual mode; or
- it writes the manual change sequence: retract `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` (or the machine file's change position), then `M6` (a stop by MP 7440 on this machine).

Also add an engine law: a post that does not handle `toolChangeMode` is refused on a manual-change machine, so other posts cannot have the same defect.

## Done means

- A two-tool job on the Picomax machine with the DIN/ISO post either refuses by name or writes a retract and a stop before the second tool cuts.
- A test pins this. Automatic-change machines are unchanged (goldens byte-identical).

Source: review of the posts against the Picomax 55 programming manual and its machine parameters. Related: #3095.

title: Field engine refuses a wide tool's short move on the per-move cell ceiling; the column engine cuts it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord when its swept window, clipped to the cut region, spans more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells. The message asks the caller to segment the move. For a wide tool, the tool's own footprint already passes the ceiling. Then a 1 mm move is refused, and segmenting cannot help.

The column engine cuts the same move. `backend.rs` says that refusals are backend-independent. This refusal is reached by a valid short move that the column arm accepts.

Measured on 6c9e5f1e7 (v0.26.0; `field_cut.rs`, `field_batch.rs` and `field_sweep.rs` are the same on main 034e91b8b), a synthetic block, cell 0.254 mm, one 1 mm feed move of a flat tool 50.8 mm across:

| Engine | Result |
|---|---|
| Column | cuts |
| Field | refused on op 0: "a chord's swept window spans more than" 1 << 22 "cells at cell size 0.254 - the move is too long for one field update; segment it" |

The tool's footprint alone is about 201 x 201 cells. With the block's height in the window, a zero-length move would pass the ceiling too.

We found it in our own lane at the same cell size: a disc head 127.4 mm across on a 44.45 mm neck (through `simulate_undercut`) and a flat tool 50.8 mm across over 33.7 mm of stock. Both were refused on their first move.

### Why it looks like a policy limit, not a memory limit

`cut_batch` keeps only a brick-to-sweep list. `cut_brick` dismisses a brick that the sweep cannot reach by one test at the brick centre. The work of a wide tool's short move is the bricks that it meets. Memory does not grow with the window.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 120.0, 120.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (60, 60, 25) to (61, 60, 25) with a flat tool of radius 25.4.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut.

### Proposed fix

Let the ceiling bound what segmenting can bound: the cells of the chord's clipped window beyond the cells of the tool at rest at the chord's start (the same clipping). A short move of any tool then passes. A long chord still refuses with the same message, and segmenting always brings it under the ceiling. Pin: the steps above cut on both engines. Keep a pin that a long chord of a normal tool still refuses.

The f32 cut twin (`cut_twin_work.rs`, `TWIN_MAX_CELLS_PER_CHORD`) states the same value. We would keep it as it is in this fix and list it as a follow-up, unless you prefer both in one change.

### Version and OS

6c9e5f1e7 (v0.26.0, source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.

body:
The Sodick LN2W post (PR #4065, issue #4045) refuses control-side wire offset. The post writes only the wire-centre path. A machine owner (Sodick AQ600L, LN2W control) gave the rules for control-side offset on 2026-11-25.

Rules from the owner:
- H numbers are consecutive integers from `H001`. A 3-pass cut uses `H001`, `H002`, `H003`. The operator sets their values at the control.
- The lead-in must be at least the wire radius long (the same rule as a mill cutter radius).
- `G41`/`G42` goes on the lead-in line, or on its own line immediately before the lead-in. The own-line form is easier.
- `G40` must go on a lead-out move.

The owner's example:

```
G54 G90
G29
T91
T84
T94
C001
G42 H001
G01 Y10.
X0.
G40 Y0
```

Open questions for the owner (ask before code):
- What does `G29` do on this control, and is it required?
- Which condition number goes with which pass (`C001` here, `C000` in the earlier kit)?

Work:
1. The post accepts compensation "in control" and "wear" for the LN2W dialect. It writes `G41`/`G42 Hnnn` on its own line before the lead-in, with H = pass number (from `H001`), and `G40` on the lead-out move.
2. The post refuses a lead-in shorter than the wire radius, with a message that names the operation.
3. The wire-centre path stays the default. Mark 21 output stays byte-identical.
4. Goldens for the square and the 2-axis parts with offset on, rough plus skims.

Done means: an LN2W program with control-side offset posts in the owner's form, a too-short lead-in is refused, and the existing LN2W and Mark 21 goldens do not change.

Refs #4045. Part of the Sodick work in #617 and #1500. Do not start before PR #4065 merges (this changes the same post).

body:
PR #4065 adds the Sodick LN2W wire post (`sodick-ln2w.cps`). The review of head `b12db2f06` found that a tapered cut on that post is not safe yet. Thus the post refuses each tapered cut by name. This issue holds the work that is necessary to post a taper again.

What is necessary before the post writes `TP` / `TN`, `G51` / `G52` `A` and `G50`:

1. **The height of the work above the worktable, for each setup.** `TP` and `TN` are heights above the worktable. A value in the machine file is the same for each setup. A 20 mm part on a 5 mm fixture then posts `TP20.` and `TN0.`, but its planes are 25 mm and 5 mm above the table. Add a setup value (a command with its MCP tool), send it in the stream, and refuse a taper when the active setup does not state it.
2. **The corner motion of the LN2W control under `G51` / `G52`.** No source confirms that the control cuts a mitre corner. A control that rounds the lower corner cuts a different surface from the surface that CamCraft checked. The owner of the AQ600L can confirm it with an air cut. Then state the confirmed rule in `sodick-aq600l.mch`.
3. **The lean side.** The app signs the stream angle by `edm.taper_angle.positive`. The post must read that rule (mirror it into `machine.edm`) and map the side to `G51` (left) or `G52` (right). Add a case for `top_right`.
4. **The angle precision.** A nonzero angle below 0.0005 degree rounds to `A0.`. Refuse it, or use a precision that the control is confirmed to read.

The removed taper code and its goldens are in the history of PR #4065 (head `b12db2f06`): `taperWord`, `taperHeights`, `edm.table_to_part_bottom` and `PARAM WireBottom`.

Refs #4045, #2130, #4065.

title: Posting holds for unchanged deficits in incoming stock

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happened

Posting can hold a program when the machined stock already has a low area in the incoming stock. This can occur when the current setup uses a casting or unfinished stock from an earlier operation. The hold can occur even when this program leaves the low area at its incoming height.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a stock mesh with a step below the surface of the nominal part.
2. Add a cut away from the step. Mark the mesh as raw stock only.
3. Post the setup. The deviation check reports the step as a gouge.
4. For a negative control, add a cut that deepens the step.

## Version and environment

Target base is CamCraft v0.26.0. The reproduction uses a synthetic stepped mesh and the headless posting tests on Windows.

## Done means

Posting holds by default. An explicit setup-session acknowledgment can permit posting if a matching stock simulation shows the same deficient cells at their incoming heights. The report gives the count, maximum depth and location. New or deeper deficits still hold posting. Reopening the project clears the acknowledgment.

Suggested triage is P3 and effort:high because this changes a posting safety check.

title: Post-merge gate: skip the full build for docs-only and process-only merges

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` runs the full batch gate on every push to `main` (`on: push: branches: [main]`, no paths filter). A merge that changes only docs (`site/`, `docs/`, `*.md`) or process files (`.claude/`) starts a full build and test run (30-60 min on a self-hosted runner) that tests exactly the code of the commit before it.

Today this is worked around outside the repo: a script on one collaborator's machine (`pm-cancel`, every 20 min) cancels such runs after they have started. That spends up to 20 runner-minutes per docs merge, depends on one machine, and other forks don't have it.

Expected: a commit that changes no code does not start (or immediately skips) the batch gate, and says so in the run summary.

Options:
1. `paths-ignore` on the push trigger (`site/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `.claude/**`), plus `workflow_dispatch` for a forced run. Simple; GitHub then shows no run for that commit.
2. A first step in the existing `yield` job (beside `post-merge-skip.sh`) that diffs the commit against its parent and sets `skip=true` when no file outside those paths changed, with a notice "docs/process only - the previous run covers this code". The run exists and is green-skipped, which keeps "one run per commit" visible.

Option 2 fits the existing skip mechanism and Sarge's "one run per commit" (#3714) best. Either way a commit that touches code, `Cargo.*`, `xtask/`, `assets/`, `.github/` or build scripts must always run the gate.

Done means: a docs-only or process-only merge to main finishes its post-merge workflow in under a minute with a "skipped: no code changed" notice; any commit touching code or build inputs runs the full gate as today; the off-repo cancel script is no longer needed.

A draft was written and reviewed with the user on 2026-11-25 (a private page; its content is summarised here so the page can be written in the docs site).

Sections:
1. **The five steps:** CAD (SolidCraft, Fusion, SolidWorks, Onshape, FreeCAD) -> CAM (CamCraft, ...) -> post (`.cps`) -> control (PathPilot, Mach3/4, LinuxCNC, grblHAL, Fanuc, Haas, Heidenhain, Siemens, Sodick LN2W) -> machine; what each hands to the next (STEP/.sc, CL data / .camproj, .nc).
2. **Conversational:** programming at the control (PathPilot conversational, Hurco WinMax, Mazatrol, Haas VPS, Sodick); when to use it and when CAD + CAM is better.
3. **Kinds of CNC machines:** mill, 4/5-axis, router, lathe, plasma, waterjet, wire EDM, sinker EDM, with example machines and what CamCraft supports.
4. **3D printing:** STL/3MF -> slicer -> printer is out of CamCraft's scope; open-source slicers (PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer, UltiMaker Cura, Bambu Studio, SuperSlicer) and commercial ones (Simplify3D; resin: Lychee, Chitubox).
5. **Design files, native vs neutral:** .sc, STEP, .f3d, .sldprt/.sldasm, Inventor/CATIA/NX, STL, DXF, SVG and what CamCraft opens directly; **Dutchman** (https://dutchmancad.xyz/, https://github.com/dutchman-cad/dutchman) converts native CAD files to SolidCraft designs.
6. **Who covers which steps:** SolidCraft + CamCraft, Fusion, SolidWorks + CAM add-in, Tormach + PathPilot, Mach3/4.
7. **Machine file (.mch) vs post (.cps):** "what can this machine physically do?" vs "how does this control want it written?"; one post serves many machines.
8. **Tools:** catalog, library, holders, tool numbers; import/export `.camtools`, PathPilot `.csv`, Hurco `.TCM`.
9. **What goes in and out of CamCraft:** part model, tools, machine, fixtures, program, project.
10. **Machine + post pairs** shipped in CamCraft (Tormach, AltMill, Haas, Heidenhain, Sodick ...).
11. **Which post do I pick?** read the control model from the control; exact match, closest dialect, air cut first, then ask on Discord / open an issue.
12. **At the machine:** load the program, set work offset and tool lengths (setup sheet), prove it (air cut, single block, feed override).
13. **How you can help:** share machine/control models, the maker's manuals, what the control accepts in your own words, alarm messages, air-cut results, machine numbers. Do not share programs or posts made by other CAM software, their screenshots or docs, or NDA material.
14. **Glossary** additions: native file, Dutchman, CL data, dialect, work offset, tool offset, pocket/tool number, single block, dry run.

Done means: a guide page "Model to Machine" with the sections above, linked from the guide index and from `machines.md`, each product claim matching what CamCraft ships at that time, `zola build` clean.

The current Sodick LN1W/LN2W controls (AQ400L, AQ600L) program taper as `G51`/`G52` with `A` and cancel with `G50`, with `TP`/`TN` for the table heights (Sodick LN1W/LN2W operation manual, Sodick Inc. 2012). A user with an LN2W machine who picks our only Sodick post gets taper words their control does not read the way the program means. The header only says "NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL"; it does not say which control the words are for.

Found when a Sodick AQ600L / LN2W owner dry-ran our kit (2026-11-25, see #1500).

Expected: the post's header (and its description in the post list) names the control it targets and states that LN1W/LN2W taper is not supported; a taper cut posted with this post states the same in its header next to the first taper word. Until the LN2W dialect (#4045) exists, that is a visible refusal-style warning instead of a silent mismatch.

Done means: every program from the Mark 21 post carries a header line naming the Mark 21 control and "LN1W/LN2W: not supported - taper words differ"; taper programs repeat it beside the first G74/G75; the post list description says the same; goldens updated; no motion or code line changes.

Refs #4045, #1500, #617.

body:
Why: our Sodick post writes the 1998 Mark 21 word set. A machine owner dry-ran our kit on a **Sodick AQ600L with an LN2W control** and reported that the Mark 21 naming does not fit his control. The public **Sodick LN1W/LN2W operation manual** (Sodick Inc., 2012; covers AQ400L/AQ600L) states the LN2W program format.

What the LN2W manual states (summary; source for the clean-room record):
- **Taper:** `G51` (left) / `G52` (right) with `A<angle per side>`, cancel `G50`; the taper starts during the move to the first surface and returns to vertical on the next XY move after `G50`. `TP` / `TN` load the Table-to-Program / Table-to-Next registers from the program. (Our post writes the Mark 21 `G74/G75` + `U V` form: wrong for LN2W.)
- **Taper heights** are control settings: Table to Limit, Upper (follows Z), Lower, Program (worktable to part bottom), Next.
- **Program start (manual example):** `G54 G90`, `G92 X0 Y0`, `G29` (reference point memory for the AWT) before `T91` (thread), `T84` (high flush), `C001`, `G41`/`G42 H001`; skim passes change `C` / `H` and use `T85` (low flush); end `M02`.
- **T codes:** T82/T83 drain closed/open, T84/T85 high/low flush, T90 cut wire, T91 thread, T96/T97 fill pump on/off.
- **Wire offset:** G40/G41/G42 with H registers per pass.

Owner notes (2026-11-25, relayed): machine is an AQ600L, control LN2W; he wants `G0 Z0` at the top "to bring the top head down" - **held until he says what Z0 is on his setup** (the manual example has no Z move; the operator sets the nozzle-gap height), because a wrong Z move can hit the upper head.

What is needed:
1. A post dialect **"Sodick LN2W"** beside the Mark 21 one (the Mark 21 post stays for older controls): the start sequence above, G51/G52 A / G50 taper, TP/TN, H registers per pass, the T codes above.
2. A machine file **Sodick AQ600L** (travels X/Y/Z/U/V and table/work limits from Sodick's published AQ600L specification; taper height keys per #2130).
3. Goldens for the EDM test parts (square, 2-axis, taper) on the new dialect, and the dry-run kit refreshed for the owner.

Not in scope: the `G0 Z0` start move (until the owner defines Z0); COND.DAT condition selection (#3183).

Done means: the AQ600L machine posts the square, 2-axis and taper test parts with the LN2W dialect - taper as G51/G52 A + G50 with TP/TN - pinned by goldens; the Mark 21 dialect output is byte-identical; the dialect header still says NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL until the owner reports a clean dry run.

Refs #1500, #2130, #617.

Part of #4023. The design record `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` (PR #4030, merged) has the side-branch plan.

## The maintainer's words

Question dialog, 2026-11-25, on "a side-branch rule in `AGENTS.md` first, and protect `side/path-kernel`": "Yes, both".

Delivery of the path kernel (question dialog, 2026-11-25): a side branch and one switch. The old behaviour stays on `main` until the new kernel is proven. No early `P1` patches go into the old planners.

## What to do

Add a short rule with a stable name (**Side branch**) to `AGENTS.md`, in the "Pull Request Law" or next to **Overlapping issues stack**. Take the content from the section "Side-branch plan" of the record. The rule says:

- what a side branch is, and that only the maintainer permits one. `side/path-kernel` is the one that exists.
- A sub-PR targets the side branch, has one issue, opens as a draft, gets the quick pass and the collaborator review as each other PR, and ends with `Refs #N` (a merge into a side branch does not close an issue).
- `main` is merged into the side branch (never a rebase, never a force-push), after each related merge batch and at least each week. A conflict in the same logic stops and goes to the maintainer.
- The gates: `post-merge.yml` covers `main` only. Each sub-PR runs the quick gate, the example catalog suites and the light lane. The side branch gets a local batch gate after each sync, inside the build limit.
- The switch-over to `main` is one PR that the maintainer approves. No agent merges it without his word.

title: Tools: a cutter hand on the tool, so a left-hand drill or mill is refused or turned M4, not run M3

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
### What are you trying to do

Keep left-hand cutters in a tool library and not run them backwards.

A left-hand drill or mill cuts only under M4. A CamCraft tool does not state its cutter hand:

- `Tool` has `thread_hand`, but that is the hand of a tap's thread (#1453).
- The Thread operation has `cutter_left` and `spindle_reverse` (#988), but these are set on the operation and both default to right-hand. A left-hand thread mill from a library therefore runs M3 until the user sets both. The #988 refusal compares the two values with each other, so it can't see what the cutter really is.
- `posting.rs` calls `ask_reverse_spindle` for the Thread operation only. I found no way to run a drill under M4.

So a left-hand drill imported from another tool library looks like a right-hand one. It posts M3, and it rubs or breaks.

This is not rare. In the public Fusion tool libraries of 45 vendor catalogues (134,498 entries), 1,333 milling and drilling tools are marked left-hand:

| Tools | Number |
|---|---|
| drills | 1,262 |
| center drills | 51 |
| multi-row thread mills | 20 |

The drills' names do not say that they are left-hand; only the library's hand field does.

I read the source at v0.26.0, and `posting.rs` and `tools.rs` on main at 49bfcaea. I did not run a left-hand tool on a machine.

### How you imagine it working

1. A `cutter_hand` field on the tool (`right` by default, `left`), for the rotating kinds. It is separate from `thread_hand`: a left-hand tap keeps its field.
2. The tool gate refuses a left-hand cutter by name for each operation that can't run M4. This step alone closes the gap.
3. The Thread operation reads the hand from the tool. `cutter_left` is then not stated twice, and the M3 refusal judges the real cutter.
4. The Drill operation runs a left-hand drill under M4 with `ask_reverse_spindle`. Posts without `millSpindleReverse` refuse it by name, as they do for #988 today (in 0.26.0, `fanuc`, `mach4`, `mazak` and `sinumerik-810m` declare it).
5. `.camtools` steps its version only for a library with a left-hand cutter, as it did for left-hand taps (`LEFT_HAND_VERSION`). An older build then refuses the file and does not read the tool as right-hand.

Steps 1, 2 and 5 are the useful first part. Steps 3 and 4 can come later.

Related: #988 (M4 thread mills), #1453 (left-hand taps), #897 (drill kinds).

Found while writing a Fusion 360 to CamCraft library converter, which skips these tools for now.

body:
**What happens now.** A Wire Contour lead goes in a straight line from the start hole to the nearest point of the wire path. On a circle, this lead is radial. The wire stops and turns at the entry point. This can leave a small dwell mark on the part.

**What we want.** An option next to the straight lead: a short tangent arc lead-in and lead-out. The lead goes from the start hole to the start of a short arc. The arc meets the contour tangentially at the entry point. The lead-out is the mirror of the lead-in. The wire then enters and leaves without a stop at the contour.

**Rules.**
- The straight lead stays the default. The arc lead is opt-in. The existing goldens do not change.
- The arc radius has a stated rule (a user value with a default, limited by the hole distance and by the kerf).
- When no tangent arc lead fits, the operation refuses by name. It does not clamp the radius silently, and it does not go back to the straight lead silently.
- The existing wire laws (the lead stays in the waste and clears the product by the kerf) and the simulation verifier check the arc lead.
- Posts: generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM write the lead arc as G02/G03. Sodick keeps its rule that the first move is straight: the move from the hole to the arc start is that straight move.
- The option has an MCP field, a project-file field (serde default; old projects do not change) and a UI row.

**Done means.**
- A die circle and a line+arc punch cut with the arc lead. The lead is tangent at the entry. The laws are clean.
- A hole that is too near and an arc that crosses the profile are refused by name.
- New post goldens for ISO, Sodick and G-EDM with the arc lead. The straight-lead goldens do not change.
- The MCP field and the project file round-trip the option.

2. Implement forward kinematics in `crates/tools` (pure rigid-frame math) and `crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs`:
   - Start from the root component's machine-side `MCS` at identity.
   - Chain each child's `MCS` onto its parent's `CSW*` port.

   - Combine STEP/STL/OBJ meshes and parametric `SpunProfile` holders into one `HolderProfile` (spindle) or `LatheClearance` (lathe).
   - Run size and tip-gap checks (`MAX_BODY_RADIUS`, `MAX_BODY_HEIGHT`, `MAX_TIP_GAP`) on the combined assembly, never on upper adapters alone.

body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582): four of the five agent runs on CamCraft **v0.25.0** (Linux x86_64 release, headless MCP) lost time or a feature to this.

## What happens

`list_operation_types` prints each kind's fields with defaults and one note: "Fields absent from the defaults are optional and off; set them in a params patch to turn them on." It never names those fields. In v0.25.0:

| kind | fields listed | accepted but not listed (found by the agents through serde errors or not at all) |
|---|---|---|
| pocket, face, contour, ... | pocket: bottom_z, clearance_z, climb, entry, feed, helix_radius, optimal_load, plunge_feed, stepdown, stepover, stock_to_leave, strategy, top_z | `tilt` (the 3+1 / 3+2 index, guide "Indexed work"), `rest` (RestDto: previous_tool_diameter, ...) |
| wire_contour | bottom_z, side, top_z | `condition` (**required**: add_operation refuses without it), `taper_deg`, `start`, `skims`, `tabs` {count, width, at, cutoff_condition}, `capture` |
| plasma_profile | bottom_z, clearance_z, comp, lead_in, lead_out, overburn, reversed, small_hole_dia, small_hole_feed, top_z | `feed`, `kerf`, `pierce_delay`, `pierce_height`, `cut_height` (unset, the posted plasma program had no F word and no M207/M208/M209) |
| drill | ... cycle ... | `cross` (see #3448); `cycle`'s values (auto, spot, drill, peck, tap, bore, back_bore, floating_tap, ream, fine_bore) |

Enum fields (`cycle`, `strategy`, `entry`, `side`, finish3d `pattern`) are typed only `"string"`.

Effect seen in the runs: q05 never found `tilt`, so it programmed the 4th-axis faces as manual re-clamp setups instead of indexed A moves; q06 had to probe `condition`, `taper_deg`, `capture` and the plasma feed/pierce fields one error at a time; q04 found `rest` only from a serde error.

## Expected

Each kind lists every field it accepts (with type, unit, default or "off", and the allowed values of an enum), so an agent can discover a feature from the tool alone. #3217 covers the wire-only part of this and the camcraft-mcp skill.

## Evidence

Agent reports: [q05 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q05-4axis/REPORT.md) (confusing-tools 4), [q06 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q06-wire-plasma/REPORT.md) problem 2, [q04 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/REPORT.md) problem 4, [q01 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q01-2d-plate/REPORT.md) (enum values).

Done means: list_operation_types names every accepted field of every kind, optional ones marked as such, with enum values listed; a test fails when a params struct gains a field the listing does not show.

title: Sodick wire: choose C conditions from the machine's own COND.DAT table

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of #617. Machine data from a Sodick owner (**Sodick AQ600L**, LN control): the machine's condition table, exported as `COND.DAT` and posted on #617 ([COND.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35214655/COND.txt), 68 KB, CRLF, unchanged). Machine data, not another CAM's output, so it is usable under the clean-room rules.

## What the table is

- 900 lines `Cnnn = f1 ... f15;`, quoted, CRLF. Header comment names the 15 fields: `ON OFF IP HRP MAO SV V SF C PIK CTRL WK WT WS WP`.
- Comment lines group the conditions by material, wire diameter and cut:

| Conditions | Section (as written in the file) |
|---|---|
| C100-C136 | WATER, SKD-11, wire 0.2 mm |
| C200-C230 | water, SKD-11, wire 0.25 mm |
| C400-C414 / C450-C479 | water, WC (carbide), wire 0.20 / 0.25 mm |
| C700-C719 / C750-C764 | water, AL, wire 0.20 / 0.25 mm |
| C800-C822 / C850-C867 | water, Cu, wire 0.20 / 0.25 mm |
| C480-C595 | 1st cut sets by wire (0.1 / 0.2 mm) and material (SKD11, WC) |
| C300-C395 | BS2, 2nd cut |
| C908-C938 / C909-C999 | BS2I-PKA, 3rd / 4th cut |
| C777, C888, C890-C893 | special (NEW4400 block) |

- `C120` appears twice with the same values.

## Why it matters now

Our post writes fixed condition numbers. The owner confirms that `C001` and `C002` **do** exist on his machine and are used for almost every pass, even though `COND.DAT` lists only `C100` and up. So the low numbers (`C000`-`C099`) come from somewhere else: written in the program, copied from this table into a working set, or a separate table. Asked on #617; his hand-written known-good program should show it. This issue must not assume a condition is missing just because it is not in `COND.DAT`.

## Wanted

- Read a `COND.DAT` (this format) into a condition library: number, the 15 fields, and the section it sits in (material, wire diameter, cut stage).
- The Sodick wire operation picks the rough and skim conditions from that library by material, wire diameter and pass, instead of fixed numbers; the post writes those numbers.
- A condition the loaded table and the working set (C000-C099, see above) both lack is refused by name before posting - only once we know where the working set comes from.
- Without a loaded table, today's behaviour stays (the header warns that each C must exist on the control).

The meaning of each field (IP, SV, WT ...) is not needed to pick by section; do not guess units for them. Ask the owner on #617 before adding his file to the repo as a test fixture; until then, a small synthetic file in the same format is enough for the tests.

Done means: a `COND.DAT` in this format loads (a test with a synthetic file in the same format, CRLF and quotes included); the 2-pass Sodick program picks its conditions from the loaded table by material, wire and pass; a condition missing from both the table and the working set is refused by name; with no table the output is byte-identical to today.

- Parse `BLOCKS` definitions and expand `INSERT` references (translation, rotation, uniform X/Y scale, row/column array grids, and `0`-layer inheritance per DXF rules).
- Enforce strict recursion depth, total expanded entity count, and cycle detection caps against block bombs. Refuse cyclic references, external references (`XREF`), non-uniform X/Y shear scaling, or tilted OCS extrusions by block/entity name.

## Done means
Dense point sampling proves flattened `SPLINE` and `ELLIPSE` polylines stay within the stated tolerance in millimeters; circular splines and ellipses keep exact `Arc`/`Circle` segments; `INSERT` expands uniform blocks (and nested blocks within limits) accurately; cyclic blocks, sheared inserts, xrefs, and malformed splines return named errors with passing fuzz tests.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
